technical_decisions: The cost is already in the Lab; it is missing from one frame only. XMage's priority() builds every option through abilityMetadata -> enrichAbilityCostFacts, and the announce_x frame raised inside that same action carries no cost at all. Remembering the chosen priority option's reported cost per seat bridges the hop with no bridge, protocol or pin change.

X is EXCLUDED from mana_cost_*: XMage holds {X} as a VariableManaCost whose own cost Mana is empty (cost = new Mana()) and whose value is fixed only after the announce (AbilityImpl.handleManaXCosts announces before expanding the cost). So the sum of the seven mana_cost_* components is the non-X mana value, which for {X}{1}{B} is 2. Corroborated by the repo's own JVM test XmageCausalStackMechanicsTest, where Sagu Mauler's {3} morph offer reads mana_cost_generic == 3 with green/blue 0 -- mana_cost_generic counts generic symbols only.

X count is not published by the bridge, so it is assumed to be 1 (as the contract directs). {X}{X} therefore budgets as a single symbol: conservative in the announcing-too-little direction, which is the safe one.

Mana budgeting is gated on _MANA_X_PROMPT_SYMBOL matching the engine's own prompt. Player.announceX serves BOTH handleManaXCosts (prompt prints {X} / 2{X}) and the non-mana announceXCost (prompt prints no mana symbol). A power/toughness or counter X is not paid in mana, so bounding it by the mana pool would be wrong. This gate is also what keeps the synthetic WS229 announce_x frames (prompt 'announce_x') on their full domain, so no WS229 assertion was relaxed.

Bounded fallback when nothing is readable: non-X cost 0 over one X symbol, i.e. the whole visible budget. Still far below 2147483647 and only ever lower than the domain allows, so the authoritative domain stays the sole validation target.

The memory is keyed on the engine's own source_object_id for EQUALITY only; it never orders, ranks or counts anything, so it cannot make same-seed fresh-process twins diverge. Last selection only, per seat, dropped on that seat's next priority decision.
A cost stated directly on the announce frame wins over the remembered one, so an engine statement is never overridden by an older one.
